ops.body:
Another occurrence, same class but a different suite — recording it here since it blocked a release gate.

**2026-08-17, daemonkit CI run 32010168325**, commit `ceb673666b77`, job `swift`:

```
✘ Test strictExecutorNonblockingReadWaitsForReadiness() recorded an issue at
  SessionReadinessTests.swift:31:6: Caught error: .systemCall(operation: "read", errno: 60)
✘ Suite SessionReadinessTests failed after 1.184 seconds with 1 issue.
✘ Test run with 67 tests in 15 suites failed after 1.184 seconds with 1 issue.
```

errno 60 is ETIMEDOUT. `SessionReadinessTests` rather than `ServiceSocketClientDeadlineTests`, but the same shape this task describes: a fixed wall-clock readiness deadline that loses under load. The run was otherwise entirely clean — 1 issue out of 67 tests, and every other suite passed including the newly added `SpawnedChannelTests`.

It had also been seen once locally the same day, under parallel suite load, passing on rerun and passing repeatedly when run alone.

Why it matters more than a nuisance now: `release.yml` calls `require_workflow CI`, so this flake is a **hard release blocker** — a single ETIMEDOUT in an untouched readiness test stops a tag from being cut, and the only remedy today is re-running the job until it wins. Worth widening the task to cover `SessionReadinessTests.swift:31` too, or fixing the whole class by driving these off an injected clock rather than wall-clock deadlines.
